card.keepWhy: Small, hidden, and it lifts everything.
sources: Matthew 13:31-32 (the Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed… the smallest of all seeds; when grown it is greater than the herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches)
Matthew 13:33 (the Kingdom of Heaven is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until it was all leavened)
Three measures (sata): roughly 20 to 40 liters of flour by common estimates, bread for a large crowd
Captions follow the World English Bible, lightly modernized

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? do you ever feel your faith, or your good, is too small to matter?
options: then these two little stories are for you.
hold that thought. jesus had something to say about small.
good. you might know someone who needs this.

steps.line: Jesus said the kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, one of the smallest seeds a farmer would plant.
steps.label: Matthew 13:31

steps.q: What do you guess that tiny seed grows into?
o: A tree with birds nesting in it
steps.why: Real mustard grows into a big shrub, a few meters tall. Calling it a tree with nesting birds was, many readers say, a playful stretch listeners would have smiled at.

steps.line: But when it grows, it’s bigger than all the garden plants. It becomes a tree, and the birds come and nest in its branches.
steps.label: Matthew 13:32

steps.line: Then another story. The kingdom is like yeast that a woman hid in three measures of flour.
steps.label: Matthew 13:33

steps.q: Three measures of flour. Roughly how much bread is that?
o: A week’s bread for one home
Bread for a hundred or more
steps.why: Estimates run from about 20 to 40 liters of flour: bread for a crowd. Sarah baked the same three measures for her three guests in Genesis 18.

steps.line: Three measures was a huge amount, enough bread for a crowd. A pinch of yeast, hidden inside, lifted all of it.
steps.label: Matthew 13:33

steps.q: Odd word: the woman hid the yeast in the flour. Bakers mix it in. Why might Jesus say “hid”?
o: Yeast was banned, so she did it secretly
The kingdom works unseen before it shows
Only she was meant to know the recipe
steps.why: Matthew’s Greek really says “hid” (enekrypsen). You never see yeast working. You only see the bread rise.

steps.line: Small, and hidden. That’s how Jesus said God’s kingdom starts.

steps.q: Elsewhere in the Bible, yeast (leaven) is usually a picture of what?
steps.why: At Passover leaven is cleared from the house, and Jesus warns of “the leaven of the Pharisees.” Here he flips it: the same spreading power works for good.

say: here’s what i love. jesus’s followers were a handful of fishermen and outsiders. by these stories, that was nothing to worry about.
christians believe God’s kingdom still grows the same way: through small, hidden acts of faith and love that slowly lift everything around them.

steps.q: Jesus’s first followers were few and unknown. Why might he tell them these two stories?
o: To warn them they’d always stay small
To say a small start isn’t a failed one
To tell them to keep their faith secret
steps.why: Small is how it starts. The seed and the yeast aren’t failing. They’re beginning.

today.say: small is how it starts. pick one tiny, hidden act today: a quiet kindness no one sees, a coin given, or a two-line prayer if you’d like: watch, learn, or join in. let it work like yeast.
options: good. no one has to know. that’s the yeast part.
lovely. two lines is plenty. small is how it starts.
